text: Catch-all routing for all request paths can use app.get('/*', handler) in Express.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 5 named wildcard matching uses app.get('/{*splat}', handler) to include the root path.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express route path with optional extension can use '/:file.:ext?' in app.get.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 5 route path optional extension should use '/:file{.:ext}' in app.get.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: An Express application supports app.del('/item', handler) as an alias for DELETE registration.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 5 removes app.del(); register DELETE handlers with app.delete('/item', handler).
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: In Express 4 req.param('id') accesses an HTTP request parameter by its name.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 5 removes req.param(); use req.params.id for route parameters.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 4 accepts res.send(204) to send a status-only response.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 5 removes res.send(status); use res.sendStatus(204) for a status-only response.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 4 supports res.redirect('/next', 301) with destination first.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Express 5 uses res.redirect(301, '/next') with status before destination.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 6 query functions support Model.findOne({email}, callback) and pass result to callback.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 7 no longer accepts query callbacks; use await Model.findOne({email}) or .then().
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 6 Model.remove(filter) is available for removing documents.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 7 removes Model.remove(); use Model.deleteOne(filter) or Model.deleteMany(filter).
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 6 exposes Model.update(filter, update) for updating documents.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 7 removes Model.update(); use Model.updateOne or Model.updateMany.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 6 permits mongoose.Types.ObjectId(hexString) without new.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 7 requires new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(hexString) when constructing an ObjectId.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 6 includes Model.mapReduce(options) for map-reduce operations.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 7 removes Model.mapReduce; use aggregation pipelines where applicable.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 6 uses strictQuery true by default and strips unknown filter properties.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: Mongoose 7 uses strictQuery false by default and keeps unknown filter properties unless configured.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 5 uses useHistory() and history.push('/dashboard') for navigation.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 6 replaces useHistory with useNavigate(); call navigate('/dashboard').
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 5 wraps matching Route elements within a Switch component.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 6 uses Routes instead of Switch for route matching.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 5 uses the Redirect component to navigate the user.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 6 replaces Redirect with the Navigate component for navigation.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 5 uses Route component={Home} or render={...} patterns.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 6 uses Route element={<Home />} instead of component or render props.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 5 provides useRouteMatch to match a pathname with route information.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 6 replaces useRouteMatch with useMatch for route matching.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 5 can put state into Redirect to={{pathname:'/profile', state:{from:'login'}}}.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide

text: React Router 6 passes state as a separate prop on Navigate, e.g. <Navigate to='/profile' state={{from:'login'}} />.
provenance: author-paraphrased from linked vendor migration guide
